1. Introduction and Architectural Scope
1.1 Purpose of the High-Level Design
This High-Level Design (HLD) document defines the software architecture, component boundaries, port interfaces, signals,
and interaction flows for the Body Control Module (BCM ECU). The BCM is responsible for managing core cabin functions
including central door locking, power window automation, exterior lighting schemes, windshield wiper/washer cycles,
immobilizer authentication, and diagnostic event recording. The architecture is formalized under Classic AUTOSAR Release
4.4.0 and targets deployment on a 32-bit automotive microcontroller with dual CAN-FD transceivers and a LIN sub-bus master
controller.
1.2 System Scope & Operational Boundaries
The scope of this document encompasses all Application Software Components (Application SWCs) located above the
AUTOSAR Runtime Environment (RTE). Basic Software (BSW) services such as the Diagnostic Event Manager (Dem),
Diagnostic Communication Manager (Dcm), CAN State Manager (CanSM), and Operating System (OS) are referenced via
standardized Service Ports and BSW bridges.
In-Scope Functional Domains:
• Central Door Locking, child lock supervision, and crash-triggered emergency unlocking.
• Smart Power Window control with express motion and anti-pinch safety algorithms.
• Exterior Lighting (headlamps, turn signals, hazard lights) and ambient illumination.
• Rain-sensing wiper intervals, high/low speed control, and washer fluid pump cycling.
• Power state transitions between Active, Standby, and Low Voltage Sleep modes.
Out-of-Scope Domains:
• Powertrain management, engine start sequence, and high-voltage battery charging.
• Hardware PCB layout schematics and low-level MCAL register definitions.
1.3 Architectural Standards & Compliance
All software specifications in this document adhere to the following normative automotive standards:
1. AUTOSAR CP R4.4.0: Component model, virtual function bus concepts, and standardized interface templates.
2. ISO 26262:2018: Road Vehicles - Functional Safety (governing safety integrity levels up to ASIL-D).
3. ISO 14229-1 (UDS): Unified Diagnostic Services on Controller Area Network.
4. ISO 11898-1/2: Controller Area Network (CAN-FD) data link layer and physical transmission.

2. System Context and Hardware Boundary
2.1 BCM Physical Context
The BCM ECU acts as the primary gateway and actuator control center for vehicular body electronics. It interfaces directly with
the central vehicle gateway over a 500 kbps / 2 Mbps CAN-FD network (Channel 1) and commands smart sub-actuators and
sensors via a 19.2 kbps LIN sub-bus (Channel 0).
Physical Transceivers & Interfaces:
• Dual high-speed CAN-FD transceivers supporting ISO 11898-2 with wake-up over bus capability.
• Single-wire LIN master transceiver compliant with LIN 2.2A.
• High-Side Smart Drivers (PROFET) for direct actuation of exterior lamps, wiper motors, and latch coils.
• Configurable analog/digital input channels with low-pass hardware filtering for door switches.
2.2 ECU Power Supply & Operating States
The module operates under nominal 12V automotive battery voltage (operating range: 9.0V to 16.0V DC). Extended crank
operating capability is maintained down to 6.0V DC for 500ms. Overvoltage protection isolates actuator stages when battery
voltage exceeds 18.0V DC.
Power Modes:
1. RUN Mode (Active): Microcontroller at 80 MHz, all SWC runnables executed periodically, full CAN/LIN transmission.
2. STANDBY Mode: Core clock reduced to 8 MHz, actuators unpowered, CAN transceiver listening for network management
frames.
3. SLEEP Mode: Deep quiescent state (< 100 µA current draw), wake-up initiated only via keyless remote or door handle pull
switch.

5.3 Core Component Functional Profiles
Profiles for DoorLockSWC, WindowCtrlSWC, LightingMgrSWC, and DiagMgrSWC:
DoorLockSWC (Safety: ASIL-B)
Functional Behavior: Central door locking, auto-lock above 15 km/h, and emergency crash unlock within 30ms.
Runnable Entities: Runnable_DoorLock_20ms (Cyclic evaluation), Runnable_DoorLock_CrashEvent (Event interrupt).
WindowCtrlSWC (Safety: ASIL-A)
Functional Behavior: Express power window motion and anti-pinch safety reversal upon force > 100N.
Runnable Entities: Runnable_WindowCtrl_20ms (Positioning loop), Runnable_PinchDetect_10ms (Current feedback).
LightingMgrSWC (Safety: ASIL-B)
Functional Behavior: Exterior headlamps, turn signal flashers, and emergency hazard flashers at 1.5 Hz.
Runnable Entities: Runnable_Lighting_20ms (Arbitration), Runnable_HazardFlash_250ms (Cadence square-wave).
DiagMgrSWC (Safety: ASIL-B)
Functional Behavior: UDS ISO 14229 services, DTC fault logging, and non-volatile freeze-frame records.
Runnable Entities: Runnable_Diag_100ms (Debounce counters), Runnable_UdsService_Handler (Diagnostic messages).

7.2 Coupling Constraints & Power Shedding Rules
1. Safety Priority: DoorLockSWC and LightingMgrSWC must prioritize signals originating from p_CrashStatus above all
convenience and user switch requests.
2. Coupling Rules: Inter-SWC communication flows exclusively through intermediate RTE buffers.
3. Power Shedding: If SupplyVoltage_mV drops below 10,500 mV, PowerMgrSWC sheds seat heaters, power windows, and
ambient lighting sequentially.

9. Functional Flow Sequences
9.1 Flow 1: Automatic Speed-Dependent Door Locking (Auto-Lock)
Precondition: Vehicle engine is running, passenger doors closed, initial speed 0 km/h.
Execution Steps:
1. Wheel speed sensors transmit periodic pulses to ABS/ESP ECU.
2. ESP ECU broadcasts velocity on CAN-FD Channel 1.
3. CanComSWC unpacks CAN frame and writes VehicleSpeedKmh to RTE port p_VehicleSpeed.
4. DoorLockSWC evaluates r_VehicleSpeed at 20ms invocation period.
5. When VehicleSpeedKmh exceeds 15 km/h:
    a. DoorLockSWC asserts output latch driver signals for all 4 doors simultaneously.
    b. Hardware solenoids energize for 120ms driving latches to LOCKED position.
    c. DoorLockSWC updates DoorLockState = 1 (LOCKED) on port p_DoorLockStatus.
6. Cluster display receives lock status confirmation and activates icon.
9.2 Flow 2: Crash Hazard Unlock and Lighting Response
Precondition: Vehicle is in motion or stationary; door latches are in LOCKED position.
Execution Steps:
1. Airbag Restraint Control Module (RCM) detects crash deceleration exceeding 5g.
2. RCM asserts discrete hardwired interrupt line PIN_03 and broadcasts Crash CAN-FD frame.
3. CanComSWC asserts p_CrashStatus.CrashDetected = TRUE within < 5ms.
4. DoorLockSWC intercepts crash event via r_CrashStatus:
    a. Overrides manual lock switch commands and child lock inhibitions.
    b. Pulses unlock solenoid drivers for 250ms to force latches into UNLOCKED state.
5. LightingMgrSWC receives emergency trigger:
    a. Immediately engages hazard flasher relays at continuous 1.5 Hz cadence.
    b. Activates interior ambient courtesy lamps at 100% brightness.
6. DiagMgrSWC registers crash freeze-frame record and locks DTC B10A2 into EEPROM.

10. Diagnostic Specifications & DTC Matrix
10.1 UDS ISO 14229 Service Support
The BCM diagnostic stack implements Unified Diagnostic Services (UDS) over ISO-TP:
• Service 0x10: Diagnostic Session Control (Default, Programming, Extended Sessions).
• Service 0x14: Clear Diagnostic Information (Group 0xFFFFFF).
• Service 0x19: Read DTC Information (sub-functions 0x02 reportByStatusMask, 0x06 reportSnapshotRecord).
• Service 0x22: Read Data by Identifier (DID read for battery voltage, software version).
• Service 0x27: Security Access (Seed-Key authentication).
• Service 0x2E: Write Data by Identifier (VIN write, end-of-line calibration).

12. Glossary and Terminology Definitions
Section 12.1: Standard Architectural Glossary
Term
Definition
SWC
Software Component: Self-contained functional unit encapsulated according to the AUTOSAR component model.
RTE
Runtime Environment: Virtual Function Bus (VFB) middleware linking SWC ports to BSW or each other.
BSW
Basic Software: Standardized software layers including Services, ECUM, Com, and MCAL drivers.
S/R Interface
Sender-Receiver Interface: Asynchronous data broadcast communication pattern between ports.
C/S Interface
Client-Server Interface: Synchronous or asynchronous operation invocation between ports.
DTC
Diagnostic Trouble Code: 3-byte identifier specifying fault classification and symptom.
ASIL
Automotive Safety Integrity Level: ISO 26262 risk classification (QM, ASIL-A through ASIL-D).
UDS
Unified Diagnostic Services: ISO 14229 protocol standard for automotive diagnostic exchange.
Section 12.2: Governance Sign-off Note
This concludes the formal High-Level Design specification for the Body Control Module. Revisions must follow formal ECN
review procedures.
